assumptions: Eisenberg's consensus scale and his plot's class boundaries.
limits: A hydrophobicity-based prediction, not a trained topology model: protein_topology is that.
Spans come from collapsing windows, so their ends are window-resolution.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which windows of this protein look transmembrane, globular or surface-seeking on an Eisenberg hydrophobic-moment plot?

description: Eisenberg hydrophobic-moment plot along a protein: per-window mean hydrophobicity and moment, each classified Globular / Transmembrane / Surface-seeking, plus those windows collapsed into residue spans. A hydrophobicity-based prediction, NOT a trained topology model.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

angle.description: rotational angle per residue in degrees: 100 for an alpha-helix (default), 160 for a beta-sheet.

minWindows.description: shortest run of same-class windows reported as a segment (default 2; a one-window run is usually noise).

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

name: protein_membrane_profile

hydrophobicity.description: mean Eisenberg hydrophobicity H per window

plot.description: the Eisenberg profile as a plot: moment and mean hydrophobicity per window

position.description: per-window class: G globular, T transmembrane, S surface-seeking

segments.description: runs of one class as 1-based inclusive residue spans, with their mean/peak moment

transmembrane.description: how many segments are classified transmembrane
